commits.edited_message:
Composite the alpha of a luma-only image directly on its Y plane

Op_flatten_alpha_plane converts its input to planar RGB, composites the
alpha plane onto the colour planes, and converts back to the source
colorspace. There is no operator from RGB back to a luma-only image, so
compositing a monochrome image with alpha failed with "unsupported color
conversion" for monochrome and RGB targets (the planner flattens first
because that is the cheapest way to drop the alpha plane) and only worked
for a YCbCr target, where the planner converts before it flattens. This
predates the per-plane ColorState.

A luma-only image (colorspace monochrome, or YCbCr with chroma
monochrome) is now composited directly on its Y plane against the BT.601
luma of the background colour, which is exact for the grey backgrounds
this feature is used with. The per-plane composite loop is shared between
the luma and the RGB path. Direct callers get errors instead of undefined
behaviour when no composition mode is set, the image has no alpha plane,
or the colour depth does not match the 'Pixel' type. The conversion entry point
already rejects an alpha plane whose geometry does not match the image.
Bayer images are declined at plan time.

Tests: monochrome to monochrome at 8 and 10 bits with exact values,
monochrome to interleaved RGB, a checkerboard, and a coloured background
that checks the BT.601 weighting.

Declare the shared colour depth in the YCbCr operators, drop the backstop

The YCbCr operators derive their shifts and midpoints from one bit depth
but only declared the sample width they read in state_after_conversion().
A YCbCr image whose planes differ in depth ('unci' declares a depth per
component) was therefore kept away from them by a blanket check at the
entry of convert_colorspace() (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), which also refused
conversions that would have been safe: Op_to_sdr_planes lowers every plane
on its own and can equalize such an image to 8 bits, as it already did for
RGB. YCbCr 16/16/8 to 8-bit RGB was refused while RGB 16/16/8 converted.

Op_YCbCr_to_RGB and the four chroma-sampling operators now require
color_channels_have_same_bpp() at plan time (their runtime guards already
returned InternalError for mixed depths), and the three 4:2:0-to-RGB
operators test the uniform colour depth instead of the luma depth alone.
With every YCbCr operator declaring the constraint, the entry check is
removed; the wider-than-16-bit backstop stays.

The GHSA-w7mc regression test keeps requiring a clean refusal for the
reporter's 16-bit target (no operator can widen the 8-bit chroma planes),
now with the generic Unsupported_color_conversion subcode, and adds the two
8-bit routes that succeed: interleaved RGB, and the native layout with
convert_hdr_to_8bit, whose samples are checked exactly.

Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa now declares only its colour-plane sample width in
the planner. Its runtime path continues to validate the alpha plane, which
keeps the planning and execution checks aligned with the other operators.

Its interleaved output state now carries alpha at the luma depth it writes,
matching the actual output storage.

Check the plane layout at the conversion and encoder entry points

The conversion operators read the planes that an image's colorspace and
chroma format imply, at the sizes they imply, and the encoder plugins do
the same. Nothing verified that the image actually has those planes. An
RGB image without its B plane failed with InternalError deep inside an
operator; a YCbCr 4:2:0 image without its Cr plane passed the pipeline as
a no-op (same layout as the encoder's request) and aborted in the x265
plugin, whose only guard is an assert that release builds compile out;
foreign planes (depth), duplicate colour planes and stray chroma planes
were silently dropped or ignored, with the outcome depending on which
operator touched them first.

HeifPixelImage::check_plane_layout() verifies that the known planes are
exactly the colour planes of the layout, optionally one separate alpha
plane on the planar layouts, and that each is present once. Colour planes
must use the size implied by their channel. Alpha is auxiliary and may
carry its own geometry, so its size is not constrained here. Planes with
channel heif_channel_unknown (the padding components of 'unci') carry no
colour meaning and are tolerated; the pipeline does not carry them into
its output. A custom colorspace has no defined layout.

The check is made at two entry points. convert_colorspace() refuses a
non-canonical image with Unsupported_image_type, and refuses custom
colorspaces, which have nothing to convert. Encoder::
check_input_image_layout() runs before the image is converted for, or
handed unchanged to, a plugin and returns a Usage_error; custom
colorspaces pass through because the uncompressed encoder writes their
components as they are. It is virtual so that an encoder can widen or
narrow it, and the plugin interface is unchanged; a plugin that supports
only a subset of the layouts still checks its input itself.

HeifPixelImage itself keeps accepting any set of planes, including several
of the same channel: multi-spectral images consist of several monochrome
planes.

The uncompressed encoder keeps sizing its output from the primary image, so a
smaller auxiliary alpha plane is accepted there as well; a larger component
remains rejected because it would write past the output buffer.

The uncompressed encoder keeps sizing its output from the primary image, so a
smaller auxiliary alpha plane is accepted there as well; a larger component
remains rejected because it would write past the output buffer. When the
auxiliary alpha image itself is encoded, its smaller Y plane is accepted only
for that input class, and the uncompressed encoder overrides the generic
layout gate because it validates its component configuration itself.

Tests: plane_layout drives the check through every canonical layout and
each kind of defect and confirms that convert_colorspace() refuses them
while tolerating unknown planes; encode_plane_layout feeds the defective
images to heif_context_encode_image through the public API.

The high-depth YCbCr-to-RGB operator now rejects only alpha planes wider
than the 16-bit samples it reads; the matching requirement remains part of
its planning state.

coupling: The defect is split over two independent composition paths. In path 1, commit 061a4682 makes ColorState::get_uniform_bits_per_pixel() return only the shared colour depth, and commit c9dcdcc5 makes Op_flatten_alpha_plane plan and execute from that helper while only rejecting alpha wider than 16 bits. A 16-bit monochrome Y plane with an 8-bit alpha plane therefore reaches a uint16_t composite that reads the one-byte alpha allocation as two-byte samples and overruns it. In path 2, commit 4ee9fa0e changes Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa planning to validate only colour-plane sample width and to report output alpha at the luma depth, and commit 5e6b8d0c relaxes its runtime alpha guard to only reject widths above 16 bits. The same source image can take mono -> YCbCr420 -> interleaved RRGGBBAA and again read the 8-bit alpha plane as uint16_t. Reverting any single edited commit leaves the other path intact: reverting 061a4682 or c9dcdcc5 leaves the YCbCr path; reverting 4ee9fa0e or 5e6b8d0c leaves the flatten path. A correct fix must restore depth agreement in both consumers (or in the shared helper and both consumers), so it is non-local.
